blocks.p: A note on this edition. This is Bunyan’s second great allegory, scene for scene, in modern English. The town of Mansoul, built by King Shaddai for his own delight, is seduced and captured by the giant Diabolus, besieged and won back by the King’s son Emmanuel, lost again through its own carelessness, and finally delivered. Nothing has been added and no episode has been removed. The sentences have been rebuilt for a reader today while keeping Bunyan’s cadence. His two prefatory poems are kept as rhymed verse. Bunyan wrote the book as one unbroken narrative; this edition divides it into titled chapters at the natural turns of the story. The edition it was made from omits his marginal Bible references, so this retelling gives a reference only where he quotes scripture outright. Speeches, trials, petitions, and charters keep every argument but lose some repetition. Most of Bunyan’s names still say exactly what they mean and are kept; the few whose meaning has worn away have been renamed, and the full list is at the back.
